s: A former wine shop in Kazimierz that became the only two-Michelin-starred kitchen in Poland.
w: Behind an unmarked wine-shop façade on Bocheńska Street, chef Przemysław Klima runs a nine-seat, reservation-only tasting menu built on foraged and fermented Polish ingredients -- birch sap, offal, lake fish. It moved from one star to two, the first Polish restaurant to do so, and books out months ahead.
_facts: Only two-Michelin-starred restaurant in Poland
Chef Przemysław Klima
Began as a natural-wine shop

s: A Kazimierz bistro and natural-wine bar built around a short, seasonal, local-produce menu.
w: On Krakowska Street toward Plac Wolnica, Nat Bistro pairs an unfussy, ingredient-first kitchen with a natural-wine list chosen bottle by bottle. Michelin gave it a Bib Gourmand and, in the 2026 guide, its Young Chef Award.
_facts: Michelin Bib Gourmand
Michelin Guide Poland 2026 Young Chef Award

s: A self-service salad-and-hot-dish counter set in the covered, heated courtyard of a medieval Old Town tenement.
w: Steps from the Main Square, Chimera fills a roofed tenement courtyard with a buffet of vegetarian salads, grains, and hot dishes sold by the item -- one of Kraków's oldest and largest canteens of its kind.
_facts: Self-service vegetarian/vegan salad bar and canteen
Housed in a covered medieval tenement courtyard

s: A home-style Polish dining room facing the Planty greenbelt, three minutes from the Main Square.
w: Under the trees of the Planty ring park, Smakołyki serves the food of a Polish grandmother's kitchen -- bigos, tripe, pork knuckle, sour rye soup, pierogi -- from breakfast onward, with live music some evenings.
_facts: Traditional/home-style Polish cuisine
Facing the Planty park

s: A twelve-seat Edomae sushi counter in Mokotów that became Poland's first Japanese restaurant to earn a Michelin star.
w: Chef Alon Than, with nearly two decades behind the knife, runs a minimalist twelve-seat counter serving omakase-only Edomae sushi -- 20 to 30 pieces built on Hokkaido scallop, Icelandic sea urchin, Spanish tuna. The Michelin Guide Poland 2026 named it the country's first Japanese restaurant to hold a star.
_facts: Poland's first Japanese restaurant with a Michelin star
Chef Alon Than
12-seat omakase-only counter

s: A Wola dining room built on the idea of 'vandalizing' traditional Polish cooking, and Michelin's pick for Opening of the Year.
w: WANDAL takes Polish comfort food apart and reassembles it with intent -- offal-stuffed doughnuts under grated horseradish, black-pudding dumplings in crayfish XO sauce -- backed by a tightly curated wine list. The Michelin Guide Poland 2026 named it the country's Opening of the Year.
_facts: Michelin Guide Poland 2026 'Opening of the Year'
Also holds a Michelin Bib Gourmand

s: A one-Michelin-star dining room on the 33rd floor of northern Poland's tallest building, looking out over Gdańsk to the Baltic.
w: Catalan chef Paco Pérez's Gdańsk outpost sits atop the Olivia Star tower, pairing Polish produce with Spanish technique and the odd Italian note -- sea views doing as much work as the plates. Holds a Michelin star.
_facts: One Michelin star
Chef Paco Pérez
33rd floor of the Olivia Star tower

s: A farm-to-table dining room in Oliwa that became the first restaurant in Poland to receive a Michelin Green Star.
w: Eliksir built its name on a zero-waste, local-and-seasonal kitchen well before that became fashionable -- a 400-bottle cellar and a produce list drawn from small Pomeranian farms. It became Poland's first Michelin Green Star restaurant.
_facts: Poland's first Michelin Green Star restaurant
Farm-to-table, zero-waste kitchen philosophy

s: A meat-forward 'butcher's bistro' near Wrocław's Rynek, from chef Beata Śniechowska.
w: Baba (full name: Baba, bistro nożownicza -- 'knife-maker's bistro') runs an offal-and-fire-driven menu from chef Beata Śniechowska and Tomasz Czechowski, formerly of the Młoda Polska group. A recent opening near the Old Town market square, already listed in the Michelin Guide.
_facts: Chefs Beata Śniechowska and Tomasz Czechowski
Listed in the Michelin Guide Poland

s: A one-Michelin-star tasting room tucked behind Między Mostami, on the Odra's bridges toward Ostrów Tumski.
w: Most ('bridge') occupies a private room at the rear of the riverside Między Mostami restaurant, running a tighter, higher-register tasting menu than its sibling out front. Holds one Michelin star.
_facts: One Michelin star
Fine-dining room behind Między Mostami restaurant

s: A dining room built into the riveted iron guts of Pszczyna's old water tower.
w: Steampunk occupies the Wodna Wieża -- a working 19th/20th-century water tower converted into a themed dining room and event space -- its brass fittings and iron stairs left exposed rather than disguised. Listed in the Michelin Guide's Silesia section.
_facts: Listed in the Michelin Guide Poland (Silesia)
Housed inside a converted historic water tower

q: Vytopna Railway Restaurant Prague Wenceslas Square
s: A miniature freight train shuttles beer, wine and food along nearly a kilometre of track laid through the dining room, crossing five working drawbridges to reach every table.
w: Since opening on Wenceslas Square in February 2010, fourteen computer-controlled locomotives haul drinks and plates from the kitchen along roughly 900 metres of track, with points and drawbridges timed to clear the way. Czech pub food is built around what the trains can carry without spilling.
_facts: 900m of model railway track, 14 computer-controlled locomotives
Opened on Wenceslas Square, February 2010

s: One Michelin star for cooking that treats old Bohemian recipes -- forcemeats, offal, wild game -- as a discipline to be recovered rather than a style to be referenced.
w: The tasting menu at this Ambiente-run dining room in a Staré Město townhouse is built entirely from pre-industrial Czech technique: pig's head, venison, freshwater fish and forgotten cuts, plated with contemporary restraint.
_facts: One Michelin star
Run by the Ambiente restaurant group

s: A minimalist, glass-fronted room on a quiet Old Town street where a single seasonal tasting menu does the talking.
w: Field holds a Michelin star for chef Radek Kašpárek's cooking, which leans on Czech ingredients -- root vegetables, freshwater fish, foraged greens -- plated in a pared-back style closer to Nordic fine dining. Near the Convent of St Agnes.
_facts: One Michelin star
Chef Radek Kašpárek

s: Two Michelin stars, awarded in December 2025, in a village restaurant surrounded by the Brdy forests twenty minutes outside Prague -- the first double star the Czech Republic has produced.
w: Chef Jan Knedla, who trained under Joël Robuchon and worked kitchens in London, Scotland, Italy, Russia and Asia, runs a tasting menu built around childhood memory and regional Bohemian ingredients, on the small square of Vysoký Újezd, a Beroun-district village rather than a Prague neighbourhood.
_facts: Two Michelin stars, awarded 11 December 2025 -- first in Czechia
Chef Jan Knedla, trained under Joël Robuchon

s: A Michelin-starred six-course tasting menu served inside a chateau built directly on the old Moravia-Austria border, deep in the Lednice-Valtice UNESCO landscape.
w: Chef Otto Vašák's restaurant occupies the Hraniční zámeček (Border Chateau) in Hlohovec, a South Moravian village near Břeclav and Valtice -- a different, much smaller place from the larger Hlohovec across the border in Slovakia. Michelin star (2025) and three Gault&Millau caps.
_facts: Michelin star awarded 2025
Housed in the Hraniční zámeček on the historic Moravia/Austria boundary
Chef Otto Vašák

s: A beer cellar reportedly over 700 years old, under a townhouse on Malostranské náměstí, a few steps from St Nicholas Church.
w: U Glaubiců serves straightforward Czech tavern food -- roast duck, goulash, dumplings -- across a street-level café, restaurant and a genuinely old vaulted cellar bar below Malá Strana's main square.
_facts: Beer cellar dates back over 700 years, per the venue
Steps from the Church of St Nicholas

s: A Vinohrady steakhouse that ages and butchers its own meat on site, serving reworked Czech classics alongside charcoal-grilled cuts.
w: U Tellerů, on Vinohradská near Jiřího z Poděbrad, runs its own dry-aging room and grills over charcoal rather than gas. The menu keeps a foot in Czech tradition (svíčková, goulash) while pushing steak cuts and modern plating to the front.
_facts: Runs its own on-site meat-aging room; charcoal grill
Listed in the Gault&Millau Czechia guide

s: A working Art Nouveau/Art Deco dining room from 1914, its walls and columns entirely tiled in ceramic mosaic, inside the Hotel Imperial.
w: Café Imperial opened in 1914 and its original decorative scheme survived intact -- hand-painted ceramic tiles, mosaic columns, coffered ceiling. Chef Zdeněk Pohlreich now runs the kitchen, serving classic Czech and Central European dishes rather than trying to modernise a room that doesn't need it.
_facts: Opened 1914; original Art Nouveau/Art Deco ceramic-tile decoration
Kitchen run by chef Zdeněk Pohlreich

s: A small bistro on Zlatnická, across from the Cosmopolitan Hotel, serving Czech dishes alongside a short flight of Czech fruit brandies.
w: XL Bistro is a newer, low-key addition near Náměstí Republiky -- easy to overlook against its five-star neighbour, but consistently well-reviewed for straightforward Czech cooking and a house selection of Czech ovocné pálenky.
_facts: Menu centres on Czech dishes plus a curated flight of Czech fruit brandies

s: A tavern-style restaurant in Kutná Hora named for Mikuláš Dačický z Heslova, the town's Renaissance-era diarist and libertine.
w: Dačický serves heavy, old-fashioned Czech food -- goulash, roast pork knee, dumplings by the plateful -- in a beamed, wood-panelled room in Kutná Hora's historic centre, near the Gothic core around St Barbara's Church. Named after Mikuláš Dačický z Heslova (1555-1626), the town's chronicler.
_facts: Named after Mikuláš Dačický z Heslova (1555-1626)
In the historic centre of Kutná Hora, a UNESCO World Heritage town

s: A working confectionery on Sedlárska, its ceiling and wall panels covered in Renaissance-style frescoes depicting Bratislava's own history.
w: Kormuth occupies rooms just off Hlavné námestie, beside the Maximilian Fountain, decorated with painted scenes covering ceilings and walls, an unusual density of decoration for a functioning café. It still operates primarily as a patisserie: cakes and coffee first.
_facts: Interior frescoes are Renaissance-style, depicting the history of Bratislava
Beside Hlavné námestie and the Maximilian Fountain
